To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the convergence of multi-agent reinforcement learning is independent of the number of interacting agents, and (ii) multi-agent reinforcement learning with many agents is guaranteed to converge even when the number is unbounded.
we propose a model-free and completely decentralized learning protocol that is scalable and provably converges to equilibrium policies in stochastic games with a large number of players.

we have developed a model-free, decentralised learning protocol that is provably convergent to Nash-equilibrium in systems with an arbitrarily large number of agents, and we have shown convergence in applications with thousands of strategically interactive agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: can we develop a scalable and decentralised learning protocol that is able to compute optimal behaviour in systems of an unbounded number, N, of strategically interacting agents?
the problem of learning in systems of many, many adaptive agents.
the question: can reinforcement learning algorithms scale to systems with many, many agents?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach can be used to solve large scale multi-agent reinforcement learning problems in a decentralized manner.
the proposed approach provides a new and powerful method for learning in multi-agent reinforcement learning, and that it is the first approach to do so that scales independently of N.
the paper presents a method to solve N-player games in which the number of agents can be very large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in systems with many, many agents, the key to successful convergence is to learn the optimal policies of each agent in isolation and then to combine these into a joint policy.
we provide the first theoretical guarantees for convergence to equilibrium policies in multi-agent reinforcement learning systems with many, many strategic agents.
we have proposed a learning protocol for multi-agent systems that is model-free, completely decentralised, and scales independently of the system size.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by leveraging the asymptotic properties of large games, it is possible to design learning protocols that scale to systems with an unprincipled number of agents and that converge to optimal behaviour.
, by using a novel learning protocol, we can achieve convergence to optimal behaviour for systems with an un-bounded number of agents.
, despite the inherent non-convexity of multi-agent reinforcement learning, there is hope for scalable learning in systems of an arbitrary number of agents.
